Heard on : 08.01.2024, 10.01.2024, 19.02.2024, 01.05.2024

Ananya Bandyopadhyay, J.:-
1.
The instant revisional application has been filed by the petitioner praying for quashing of the
proceedings of G.R. Case No. 02 of 2011, pending before the Court of the Learned Additional Chief
Judicial Magistrate, Kalyani which arose out of Chakda Police Station Case No. 591/2010 dated
29.12.2010 under Sections 272/273 of the Indian Penal Code.
2.

The allegations in the complaint dated 29.10.2010, inter alia, elucidated the opposite party no. 2 to have purchased two Lactogen - I infant food packets from Sathi Stores, of Chakda Bus Stand on 12.12.2010.
After purchasing the said infant food the opposite party no. 2 fed the same to his twin babies.
Subsequently, the opposite party no. 2 noticed the remaining portion of the contents in the said packet contained small insects.

Consuming the contaminated infant food the babies of the opposite party no. 2 got ill and subsequently the opposite party no. 2 took his babies to Dr. Dipak Tapash Chaki vs The State Of West Bengal And Anr on 2 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148347040/

sentences.text: 1 Das Roy according to whom the adulterated infant food sickened the babies.

After returning from doctor's chamber the opposite party no. 2 opened the second packet and after opening the same,
noticed more insects in that packet also.
Thereafter the opposite party no. 2 informed the police of the retailing shop from which the said food product was purchased.
The staff of the said shop asked the opposite party no. 2 to deposit the said packet for sending the same for test.
However, the opposite party no. 2 did not agree to hand over the said packet to the staff of the said shop.
Subsequently on 29.12.2010 the officers from Nestle India Ltd. met the opposite party no. 2 and asked for the said packets as they would be sending the same to the laboratory for test.
The officers also informed that they would be handing over the result of the forensic test of the product to the opposite party no. 2 apart from which they will not be able to do anything.

3. After initiation of the impugned proceeding the petitioner duly surrendered before the Court of the Learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Kalyani 06.01.2011 and was thereafter released on bail by the Learned Magistrate on the same day.

entities.text: Court of the Learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Kalyani
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 4. After completion of a purported investigation the Investigating Agency submitted its report in final form vide Charge Sheet No.301 dated 30.6.2011 under Sections 272/273 of the Indian Penal Code against the petitioner.
5. Upon receiving the report in final form the Magistrate took cognizance of the same and committed the case to the Court of Session trial.

6. From a bare perusal of the laboratory test report submitted by Dr. A. Dutta Gupta, Public Analyst (Food & Water) West Bengal it transpired that the doctor failed to opine whether the said infant milk food was adulterated at the time off its production.
The said report did not mention that the sample was sent to the laboratory after complying the necessary requirements for sampling the product.
Dr. Duttagupta in his report stated that the said sample was not sent following the prescribed guidelines.
It transpired from the said report that the sample was sent in an unsealed packet tied with rubber band placed in a labeled open hard paper packet, the inner packet was tied with a rubber band.
Moreover, the open packet was neither kept in a sterilized container, nor the sample was supplied maintaining cold chain.

From the report submitted by the Analyst it was clear that the said doctor was of the opinion that the - "Analytical result described in the report reveals the condition of the sample at the time of analysis.
Condition of the sample particularly micro biological condition at the time of sampling could not be assessed from the analysis due to long gap in between the date of sampling and date of analysis.
The manner in which sample has been preserved during the period is not suitable to predict the microbial condition at the time of sampling.
Hence not fit microbial analysis.
However, microbial analysis was performed to assess the present microbial condition.
So presently the sample does not conform to the standard as laid down for infant formula in Item No. A.11.02.13.31 of Appendix (b) of PFA Rules, 1955 (amended) due to presence of yeast and mould.
Hence under present condition the sample is adulterated under sub clause (a), (b), (e) & (l) of Clause Investigating Agency of Section 2 of the P.F.A. Act, 1954.
Again this opinion may not reflect the condition of the sample at the time of sampling".

sentences.text: Petitioner further submitted the scheme of law of the land expressed that, the procedural Code generally governed matter but if a Special or local Law was in force, covering the same area, the later would prevail over the Code.

In the instant case the Learned Magistrate was pleased to take cognizance in a mechanical manner without applying judicial mind that the said offence as disclosed in the First Information Report could only be attracted under the provision as laid down under the Prevention of food Adulteration Act, 1954.

In such circumstances, the Learned Magistrate committed grave error in law by taking cognizance of the offences under Sections 272/273 of the Indian Penal Code, brushing aside the fact that Special Law i.e. Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,
enacted for the purpose of the said offence was already under force.
8. From the report submitted by the Public Analyst it was clear that the Public Analyst failed to opine the adulteration of the product prior to the time of sampling.
Moreover, the opposite party failed to produce any medical documents relating to the treatment of his babies which further cast a grave shadow of doubt over the veracity of the prosecution case.

9. Considered the submissions of the Learned Advocate for the petitioner as well as the State.
10.
It is a well settled principle of law that when any law is silent on certain procedures, similar procedures or conditions as laid down in other equivalent Acts are required to be followed.
The Code of Criminal Procedure as also the Indian Penal Code is silent relating to procedures for enquiry and/or investigation with regard to offences relating to adulteration of food.

However, the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 enacted for the purpose of offences relating to adulteration of food provides the in details procedures for enquiry, investigation, initiation of proceedings before court relating to such offences and as such the law as laid down under said Act gains importance.

Section 13 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 provides that upon receipt of the report of the result of the analysis the local (health) authority shall forward a copy of the report of the result of the analysis to such person as disclosed under section 14A of the said Act,
informing such person that he may make an application before the court within a period of 10 days from the date of receipt of copy of the report, that the article of food kept by the local health authority be analysed by Central Food Laboratory.
However, in the instant case such copy was not forwarded by the Court as also the local health authority in compliance with the said provision.

Moreover, it is apparent from the materials on record that the procedure as laid down under Section 11 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act has not been complied for obtaining sample of the food.
11. Section 272 of the Indian Penal Code provides that "whoever adulterates any article of food or drink, so as to make such article noxious as food or drink, intending to sell such article as food or drink, or knowing it to be likely that the same will be sold as food or drink.....".

The ingredients required for this provision of law are i) that the food or drink had been adulterated, ii) the accused person had adulterated the food or drink and iii) the accused had intended to sell such food or drink.
In order to bring home the charge the most the most essential requirement was to discover the person who had adulterated the food or drink.
For such reasons the legislature in its wisdom had given importance to the word "Whoever" as the intention of legislature is to find out the person responsible for such adulteration.

However, in the instant case it transpired from the report of the Tapash Chaki vs The State Of West Bengal And Anr on 2 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148347040/
3 Public Analyst (Food and Water) that the sample which was sent for examination to the laboratory did not specifically reflect the stage when the said food was adulterated.

sentences.text: Moreover, from the report it revealed due to improper sampling of the article it could not be ascertained whether the article was adulterated at the time of sampling.
Moreover, it was not apparent from the First Information Report that food was kept by the opposite party no.2 in the prescribed manner, as the same was required to be kept after removal of the seal.
In such circumstances, when the stage of such adulteration could not be ascertained or the person responsible for such adulteration be identified.

12. Section 273 of the Indian Penal Code provides that "Whoever sells, or offers or exposes for sale,
as food or drink, any article which has been rendered or has become noxious, or is in a state unfit for food or drink, knowing or having reason to believe that the same is noxious as food or drink...."
The vital ingredient for the purpose of section 273 of the Indian Penal Code is to ascertain as to the knowledge of the seller of such article being noxious.
In the instant case it did not transpire that the infant food was noxious at the time when it was sold from the store of the petitioner.
The investigating agency had not seized sealed packets of similar batch nos. to get it compared with the contents of the unsealed packets.
It could not be proved on the basis of materials on record that for was adulterated or noxious.
The impugned proceeding will be harassive in nature and will result in the process of abuse of law, if allowed to be continued.

13. In view of the above discussions, the proceedings of G.R. Case No. 02 of 2011, pending before the Court of the Learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Kalyani which arose out of Chakda Police Station Case No. 591/2010 dated 29.12.2010 under Sections 272/273 of the Indian Penal Code is quashed.

15. There is no order as to costs.
